text: Keyholder shall decide every command that reaches an actuator from a written authority table, with one arbiter that runs unchanged in simulation and against the wall clock.
rationale: The person asked for des as the engine of control software for something they build. Whatever they build, more than one thing will want to move it.

text: Authority over each actuator shall be data that a person can read, not an order of calls in code.
rationale: A rule nobody wrote down cannot be amended or blamed; it is whoever's code ran last.

text: The arbiter shall be the only code path that calls an actuator's driver.
acceptance: T-TABLE-ONLY passes: (a) a source scan finds no driver call outside keyholder.mjs; (b) a driver called without the arbiter's private token throws.
rationale: Sketch: with one extra direct writer (a boost button), the heater ran on a dead sensor in 76.5% and 80.5% of trials (seeds 1-200, 1001-1200), p50 148 s and 240 s.

text: The arbiter shall refuse to start with a table that names an unknown source or actuator, lacks a safe state for an actuator, or ranks any non-safety source above a safety source.
acceptance: T-TABLE-REJECT passes: each of 4 malformed fixture tables throws at construction, naming the offending entry; the 2 shipped tables load.
rationale: The table is the rule; a rule that contradicts itself must fail before the relay closes, not after.

text: A safety demand shall outrank every other source.
rationale: Therac-25: the software interlock was trusted to replace the hardware one, and its order of operations decided who lived.

text: While a safety latch is held, the arbiter shall keep its actuator in the declared safe state whatever other sources command.
acceptance: T-SAFE-OUTRANK passes: 1000 seeded random command sequences over both plants, zero instants with a latched actuator outside its safe state.
rationale: Sketch: 0 trials of 400 with heater on after the latch, against 314 of 400 under last-writer-wins.

text: The arbiter shall apply a safety demand at the sim instant the demand is raised.
acceptance: T-SAFE-PROMPT passes: a latch raised at t while another source holds the actuator on gives the safe state at t, with no other source asking.
rationale: My sketch's first draft set the latch flag and waited for the next request; a boost already running kept heating a dead bath in 3-4% of trials, up to 120 s.

text: A latch shall be lifted only by an operator reset received while every permissive the table names for that actuator holds.
acceptance: T-SAFE-RESET passes: a reset with a stale reading is refused and logged with the failing permissive; a reset with fresh readings lifts the latch; no other source lifts it.
rationale: Who may undo a safety decision is the most important line in the table; it must name a person, not a timer.

text: Every decision the arbiter makes shall be logged with its reason and shall replay.
rationale: A refusal the operator cannot read looks like a broken machine; one they can read is a rule they can argue with.

text: Each actuator change and each refused command shall produce one log entry naming the source, the command, and the table rule that decided it.
acceptance: T-LOG-REASON passes: in 20 seeded runs, actuator changes equal change entries one for one, and every refusal names a rule id present in the table.
rationale: Sketch: 666 and 756 boost refusals in 200 trials each, all while the sensor was dead. Each one is the operator being told something true.

text: A decision log from a fake-clock realtime run shall replay under run() to identical decisions.
acceptance: T-LOG-REPLAY passes for both plants, and fails when one logged reading is altered.
rationale: Stopwatch's harness, reused: the log is the evidence that the running code is the tested code.

text: The arbiter and table format shall not be shaped by one plant.
rationale: We do not know what they build. The authority layer is the part that survives that answer.

text: The same arbiter shall hold a second plant, a motor-driven gate with two end-stops and an emergency stop, using only a second table.
acceptance: T-PLANT-GATE passes: zero steps driven past a tripped end-stop, jog refused while the e-stop is held, and keyholder.mjs unchanged between plants.
rationale: A heater is one-sided (off is safe). A motor is two-sided (stopping is safe; neither direction is). If the table only works one-sided it is bath-shaped.

text: The suite shall run the last-writer-wins arrangement as a negative control and shall fail it.
acceptance: T-NEG-LWW passes: the T-SAFE-OUTRANK property, run against last-writer-wins, finds a violation within 1000 sequences.
rationale: A property test that cannot fail the arrangement it replaces proves nothing about the one it keeps.

text: The installed machine shall have a cutout that no software path can command.
acceptance: The person records, with a photograph of the wiring, a thermal fuse or limit switch in series with the actuator's power, outside the computer's reach.
rationale: Keyholder decides between programs. It must not become the last line; a fuse does not run JavaScript. Unverifiable here, and reported as unverified.
